stories.headline: Iran hits Kuwait's largest refinery, escalates strikes across Gulf energy infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Iran launched drone strikes on Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery, the country's largest, which processes approximately 730,000 barrels of oil per day. Fires broke out across multiple units on March 20 as Kuwaitis marked Eid al-Fitr, marking the second consecutive day the facility was targeted.
key_facts.excerpt: Fires broke out across multiple units at the Mina al-Ahmadi refinery, which processes about 730,000 barrels of oil per day, early on Friday morning, as Kuwaitis marked Eid al-Fitr.

key_facts.fact: Qatar's energy minister said the country's LNG export capacity will be reduced by 17% over the next five years due to Iranian attacks on the Ras Laffan facility, representing an estimated $20 billion annual revenue impact and a 3-to-5-year repair timeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatar's energy minister says its liquefied natural gas export capacity will be reduced by 17% over the next five years as a result of an Iranian attack on the Ras Laffan facility.

key_facts.fact: An Iranian drone struck a Saudi Aramco refinery in Yanbu on the Red Sea, a joint venture with ExxonMobil, while the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia all reported additional missile or drone attacks on March 19-20.
key_facts.excerpt: An Iranian drone struck a Saudi Aramco refinery in Yanbu, on the Red Sea, on Thursday, according to the Saudi Ministry of Defense.

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned of 'zero restraint' if Iranian energy facilities face further attack, claiming previous strikes represented only a 'fraction' of Iran's capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated the nation would show 'zero restraint' if additional infrastructure is struck, claiming their previous response used only a 'fraction' of their capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude spiked above $119 per barrel early on March 19 before settling at $108.65, up 1.18%. European gas benchmark surged approximately 12%. The US government took steps to expand supply as President Trump looked toward November midterm elections.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude oil prices, a benchmark for global trading, climbed about 2%, hitting nearly $110 a barrel for contracts to purchase oil in May. The price rose as high as $119 early Thursday but pared some of its gains by the afternoon.

stories.headline: Israel strikes Tehran on Nowruz after Netanyahu pledges to halt South Pars attacks at Trump's request

key_facts.fact: Israel pounded Tehran with airstrikes on March 20 as Iranians marked Nowruz (Persian New Year), one day after Prime Minister Netanyahu pledged to 'hold off' further attacks on Iran's South Pars gas field at President Trump's request.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel pounded Tehran with airstrikes Friday as Iranians marked Nowruz, or the Persian New Year. The attacks came a day after Israel pledged to refrain from more strikes on a key Iranian gas field.

key_facts.fact: Heavy explosions shook Dubai early on March 20 as the conflict risked drawing Iran's Arab neighbors directly into the war, with the UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Bahrain all reporting missile or drone attacks on their territory.
key_facts.excerpt: Overnight, blasts have been heard in Jerusalem and in the Iranian capital Tehran as Iranians mark Nowruz. The United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain all reported missile or drone attacks.

key_facts.fact: Iran told the UK that allowing the US to use British military bases would be considered 'participation in aggression,' according to the Iranian foreign ministry, escalating diplomatic pressure on London.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran tells the UK that allowing the US to use British military bases will be considered 'participation in aggression', according to the Iranian foreign ministry.

key_facts.fact: The conflict's death toll has reached over 1,300 in Iran and 13+ US military personnel. Israel reported 15 deaths from Iranian missiles. Over 1 million people have been displaced in Lebanon according to the Lebanese government.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran deaths: 1,300+. Israel deaths: 15 from Iranian missiles. US military deaths: 13+. Lebanon displacement: 1+ million.

stories.headline: Trump administration weighs deploying thousands of US troops as Iran war enters new phase

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration is considering deploying thousands of additional US troops to reinforce operations in the Middle East as the Iran war enters its third week, according to a US official and three people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump's administration is considering deploying thousands of U.S. troops to reinforce its operation in the Middle East, as the U.S. military prepares for possible next steps in its campaign against Iran.

key_facts.fact: Options under consideration include securing safe passage for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz using air and naval forces, as well as deploying ground forces to Iran's shoreline and potentially to Iran's Kharg Island, the hub for most of Iran's oil exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Those options include securing safe passage for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. But securing the Strait could also mean deploying U.S. troops to Iran's shoreline. The Trump administration has also discussed options to send ground forces to Iran's Kharg Island.

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters on March 19 that he is 'not putting troops anywhere,' contradicting the internal deliberations reported by Reuters. Deployment of ground forces could anger parts of Trump's political base opposed to new Middle East entanglements.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump told reporters he's 'not putting troops anywhere' after being asked about the possibility of deploying additional troops.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon is seeking an additional $200 billion for Iran war operations. The US military has been primarily conducting air and naval operations since the war began on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon is seeking an additional $200 billion for Iran war operations.

stories.headline: Kremlin confirms Ukraine peace talks on 'situational pause' as Iran war diverts US attention

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed on March 19 that talks between Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv on ending the war in Ukraine are on a 'situational pause, for obvious reasons' following the start of the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The three-way group is on hold,' Dmitry Peskov, Russian President Vladimir Putin's spokesperson, told the Izvestia newspaper Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The last trilateral meeting was in February in Geneva. A new round of talks scheduled for March 5 in Abu Dhabi was postponed indefinitely, days after the US and Israel launched the attack on Iran on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The last time the three parties met was in February in Geneva. A new round of talks scheduled for March 5 in Abu Dhabi was postponed indefinitely, days after the U.S. and Israel launched an attack on Iran.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy told the BBC he had a 'very bad feeling' about the Iran war's effect on Ukraine negotiations, saying talks were 'constantly being postponed.' However, he also said new discussions were expected over the weekend and that Washington had sent signals it was ready to continue.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said he had a 'very bad feeling' about the effect of the events in Iran on the war in Ukraine. Negotiations, he said, were 'constantly being postponed. There is one reason: [the] war in Iran.'

key_facts.fact: Russia's Izvestia reported the Kremlin believes the Iran war could push Kyiv towards compromise. Economic cooperation talks between Moscow and Washington, led by envoy Kirill Dmitriev who has discussed joint projects worth up to $14 trillion, will continue alongside prisoner swap negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev has previously suggested the two sides were eyeing joint projects worth up to $14 trillion. Russia has also long been lobbying for the United States to lift economic sanctions.

stories.headline: Super Micro co-founder charged with smuggling $2.5B in Nvidia AI chips to China

key_facts.fact: Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw and two others were charged on March 19 with conspiring to divert $2.5 billion worth of servers containing Nvidia AI chips to China in violation of US export control laws, according to an indictment unsealed in Manhattan federal court.
key_facts.excerpt: The co-founder of Super Micro Computer and two others were charged with diverting $2.5 billion worth of servers with Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips to China, in violation of US laws barring exports to that country without a license.

key_facts.fact: The scheme involved sending US-made servers through Taiwan to other countries in Southeast Asia, where they were swapped into unmarked boxes and sent onward to China. Defendants used fabricated documents and staged bogus equipment to pass audit inventories.
key_facts.excerpt: A complex scheme to send US-made servers through Taiwan to other countries in Southeast Asia, where they were swapped into unmarked boxes and sent on to China.

key_facts.fact: Liaw, who co-founded Super Micro in 1993 and controls $464 million worth of company shares, was arrested in California and released on bail. Co-defendant Ruei-Tsang 'Steven' Chang, who worked in Super Micro's Taiwan office, remains at large. Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun, a contractor, is detained.
key_facts.excerpt: Liaw, who co-founded Super Micro Computer and served on its board of directors, was arrested Thursday in California and released on bail. Chang remains at large. Sun is held awaiting a detention hearing.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro shares fell approximately 12% in extended trading. The company placed Liaw and Chang on administrative leave, terminated its relationship with Sun, and said it maintains a 'robust compliance program.' Super Micro itself was not named as a defendant.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer is not named in the indictment. The company released a statement saying it has placed Liaw and Chang on administrative leave and terminated its relationship with Sun.

stories.headline: HSBC weighs cutting 20,000 jobs over 3-5 years as CEO bets on AI to reshape operations

key_facts.fact: HSBC is weighing deep job cuts that could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles, or about 10% of its 208,720 full-time equivalent workforce, as part of a multi-year AI-driven restructuring under CEO Georges Elhedery, according to Bloomberg News.
key_facts.excerpt: HSBC Holdings Plc is weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery bets on AI to shrink its middle and back offices. The changes could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles — or about 10% of its total workforce.

key_facts.fact: Non-client-facing roles in global service centers are expected to be most impacted. The plan spans three to five years and could include not replacing departing staff as well as cuts tied to business exits or sales. The assessment is at an early stage with no final decisions made.
key_facts.excerpt: Non-client facing roles in global service centers are among those expected to be most impacted although the assessment is at an early stage.

key_facts.fact: CFO Pam Kaur said HSBC aims to deploy AI across customer service, transaction monitoring, and compliance processes including know-your-customer protocols. Hong Kong-listed HSBC shares fell 2.2% following the report.
key_facts.excerpt: CFO Pam Kaur said the bank aims to deploy AI across key areas such as customer service, transaction monitoring, and compliance processes including know-your-customer protocols.

key_facts.fact: Analysts predict global banks could eliminate up to 200,000 roles in coming years as digital adoption accelerates, with an average 3% workforce reduction across the industry. HSBC's plan would be among the largest AI-driven layoffs in the banking sector.
key_facts.excerpt: Global banks could eliminate up to 200,000 roles in coming years as digital adoption accelerates, with analysts predicting an average 3% workforce reduction across the industry.

stories.headline: Crypto.com lays off 12% of staff as CEO warns AI shift is 'do or die' for companies

key_facts.fact: Crypto.com cut approximately 180 employees, representing 12% of its roughly 1,500-person workforce, on March 19 as part of a company-wide pivot to enterprise AI integration.
key_facts.excerpt: The exchange laid off about 180 employees as it restructures and rolls out enterprise-wide AI to drive efficiencies.

key_facts.fact: CEO Kris Marszalek warned that 'companies that do not make this pivot immediately will fail' and that those moving slowly would be 'left behind.' He said firms pairing 'the best AI tools with top performers will achieve a level of scale and precision that was previously impossible.'
key_facts.excerpt: Companies that do not make this pivot immediately will fail. Companies that move slowly will be left behind. Companies that move immediately and pair the best AI tools with top performers will achieve a level of scale and precision that was previously impossible.

key_facts.fact: In February 2026, Marszalek purchased the ai.com domain for $70 million, signaling deeper strategic commitment to AI. Crypto.com previously conducted a 20% workforce reduction in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: In February 2026, Marszalek purchased the ai.com domain for $70 million, signaling the company's commitment to artificial intelligence expansion.

key_facts.fact: The Singapore-based exchange recently received conditional approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, enabling expanded federal custody services, even as it reduces headcount.
key_facts.excerpt: The exchange secures conditional U.S. approval to launch a federally regulated crypto trust bank.

stories.headline: FDA approves Wegovy HD (7.2mg), delivering ~21% weight loss in fastest GLP-1 approval yet

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Wegovy HD (semaglutide 7.2mg injection) on March 19 for weight loss in adults with obesity, marking the fourth approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program. The decision came just 54 days after filing, a record pace.
key_facts.excerpt: The decision was granted just 54 days after filing and represented the fourth approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program.

key_facts.fact: In the STEP UP trial, Wegovy HD achieved average weight loss of approximately 20.7% at 72 weeks in adults with obesity, compared to ~15% for the standard 2.4mg dose. About one in three participants achieved 25% or greater weight loss.
key_facts.excerpt: In the STEP UP trial, about one in three trial participants taking Wegovy HD achieved 25% weight loss or higher. Average weight loss of ~21% at 72 weeks in adults with obesity.

key_facts.fact: FDA Commissioner Martin Makary said: 'The new FDA is moving with unprecedented efficiency on products that advance national priorities. Today's approval is another demonstration of what the FDA can accomplish when we try bold new things.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The new FDA is moving with unprecedented efficiency on products that advance national priorities. Today's approval is another demonstration of what the FDA can accomplish when we try bold new things.'

key_facts.fact: Novo Nordisk expects to launch the 7.2mg dose in April. The higher dose positions Wegovy to better compete with Eli Lilly's Zepbound, which has proven more effective at promoting weight loss than standard Wegovy. Dysesthesia (altered skin sensation) occurred more frequently at the higher dose (22.9%).
key_facts.excerpt: Dysesthesia occurred markedly more often at 7.2 mg (22.9%); symptoms typically resolved, and the FDA is investigating this signal.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly's triple-agonist retatrutide clears first Phase 3 trial with up to 17% weight loss

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly announced positive topline results from TRANSCEND-T2D-1, the first Phase 3 trial of retatrutide, a first-in-class GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist, in 537 patients with Type 2 diabetes over 40 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Eli Lilly and Company today announced positive topline results from TRANSCEND-T2D-1, a Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of retatrutide, an investigational first-in-class GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist.

key_facts.fact: Retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 1.7% to 2.0% across doses at 40 weeks (vs. 0.8% placebo). At the 12mg dose, patients lost an average 16.8% of body weight (36.6 lbs), with no weight loss plateau observed through 40 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 1.7% to 2.0% across doses at 40 weeks. Participants taking retatrutide 12 mg lost an average of 36.6 lbs (16.8%). No weight loss plateau was observed.

key_facts.fact: The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal: nausea (16-27% vs. 4% placebo), diarrhea (19-26% vs. 5% placebo), and vomiting (15-18% vs. 2% placebo), primarily during dose escalation. Dysesthesia occurred in 2-5% of patients.
key_facts.excerpt: Most common adverse events included nausea (16.4%-26.5% vs. 3.7% placebo), diarrhea (18.7%-26.3% vs. 4.5% placebo), and vomiting (15.0%-17.6% vs. 2.2% placebo).

key_facts.fact: Detailed results will be presented at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions in June. Additional Phase 3 results are expected over the next year. Lilly is betting on retatrutide as the next pillar of its obesity portfolio after Zepbound and upcoming oral drug orforglipron.
key_facts.excerpt: Detailed results will be presented at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions in June; additional Phase 3 results expected over the next year.

sources.title: Lilly's triple agonist, retatrutide, demonstrated significant reductions in A1C and weight in first Phase 3 trial

stories.headline: J&J's icotrokinra becomes first targeted oral treatment for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Johnson & Johnson's ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), the first and only oral peptide targeting the IL-23 receptor, for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients aged 12+ weighing at least 40 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: Johnson & Johnson announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), an interleukin-23 (IL-23) receptor antagonist for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

key_facts.fact: In the ICONIC clinical program involving 2,500 patients across five Phase 3 studies, approximately 70% achieved clear or almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) at Week 16, and 55% achieved PASI 90 response (90%+ improvement). The safety profile was comparable to placebo within 1.1% difference.
key_facts.excerpt: ~70% achieved clear/almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) at Week 16. 55% achieved PASI 90 response (≥90% improvement) at Week 16. Safety profile comparable to placebo.

key_facts.fact: Head-to-head studies demonstrated superiority versus both deucravacitinib and ustekinumab. Until now, targeted biologics for psoriasis required injections; icotrokinra is taken as one tablet daily.
key_facts.excerpt: Head-to-head studies demonstrated superiority versus deucravacitinib and ustekinumab. ICOTYDE uniquely offers oral administration versus injectable biologics.

key_facts.fact: J&J EVP Jennifer Taubert called the approval 'a transformative shift in plaque psoriasis management.' Dr. John Reed (J&J R&D) said icotrokinra represents 'a fundamentally different treatment with potential to redefine patient expectations.'
key_facts.excerpt: Jennifer Taubert: 'marks a transformative shift in plaque psoriasis management.' Dr. John Reed: 'a fundamentally different treatment with potential to redefine patient expectations.'

sources.title: FDA approval of ICOTYDE (icotrokinra) ushers in new era for first-line systemic treatment of plaque psoriasis
FDA approves icotrokinra, first oral peptide for adults and teens with plaque psoriasis
